utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everybody. Could the registrar please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-03-69-PT, the Prosecutor versus Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Would the parties make their appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: For the Prosecution David Re, trial attorney, with the Prosecutor Madam Carla Del Ponte, assisted by our case manager, Ms. Carmela Javier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I have to note this hearing is conducted via videolink. Before going on further, I have to check whether the parties in Belgrade can follow us. Can I ask Mr. Jovanovic to confirm this.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I can hear you very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Then can I have the appearances from the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Geert-Jan Knoops, counsel for Mr. Stanisic, Ms. Tanja Radosaveljevic, legal consultant of our team. She is currently present with the accused in Belgrade, Mr. Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Knoops. And Mr. Jovanovic, could you introduce yourself and your accused again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Good afternoon, Your Honour. My name is Zoran Jovanovic, attorney-at-law from Belgrade, and I am appearing for the accused Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Jovanovic. I have to note that at the outset this hearing, which was originally scheduled to take place on Monday, 13th of March, had to be postponed due to certain logistical problems that are beyond the control of the Chamber, to take place today. On 16th of December, 2005, the Trial Chamber issued its decision on Prosecution motion for leave to amend the amended indictment granting the Prosecution's motion to amend again the indictment to include new charges related to events in and around Srebrenica. Since the Chamber denied the Defence request for certification for appeal against this amendment, the amendment has been finalised subject to further consideration on the challenge on the form of indictment the Trial Chamber is currently seized of. So therefore, having said that, the accused need to enter a plea on the new charges in the amended indictment, and that's why we are having a hearing today, for the purpose of further appearance of the accused pursuant to Rule 50(B) of the Rules. So, Mr. Knoops and Mr. Jovanovic, it is the right of the accused to have the indictment read out in full in a language they understand. Do they wish to have the new charges in the indictment read out in full?

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the accused in our case waives his right to have the indictment read out in full. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you, Mr. Knoops. Mr. Jovanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Mr. Simatovic also feels it is not necessary to have the indictment read out in full. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Very well, Mr. Jovanovic. Before we have a plea from the accused, I have to make sure with the Prosecution as to the counts which should be applied to this new indictment. What is added in the new indictment -- is added to this current indictment is the new factual allegations related to in and around Srebrenica. Although they are appearing in paragraphs which is related to murder, but that factual allegation is related to all the other counts. In other words, all five counts should apply to this allegation. Am I correct in so understanding?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The allegations are related to the counts murder, number 2, murder, a crime against humanity; and murder, number 3, a violation of the laws or customs of war; and Count 1, which is persecutions. They don't relate to Counts 4 and 5, which is deportations and inhumane acts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can I have the indictment, legal officer? Can I bring your attention, Mr. Re, to the paragraph 21 of the indictment, amended indictment. 21 (a) refers to paragraphs 23 to 67, which include the allegation in relation to Srebrenica. And the same is true with other counts. I should have made clear before this further appearance. I wonder whether you are in a position to answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, what is the question, if I could clarify, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Paragraphs from 19 to 22 deals with the counts of persecutions. In setting out the factual allegation, you refer to murder of people as described in paragraphs 23 to 67, which includes the allegation related to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So you indicted -- you wish to indict these accused on the count of persecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In relation to the allegation in relation to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's quite correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But could you check what you answered? Let me take a look. Could you take a look at paragraph 68. So Counts 4 and 5 deal with deportation and inhumane acts; i.e., forcible transfer. But you included there the word of -- the name of Srebrenica there. So I wanted to clarify your position.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I understand now entirely Your Honour's point. No, if the word Srebrenica is there in the last count, it's not intended to relate to these --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you speak up a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's not intended to relate to these particular fresh allegations. Counts 1, 2 and -- I put it the other way around. The new charges from the Srebrenica video relate to Counts 1, persecution; Counts 2 and 3 which are both murder, but not Counts 4 and 5. I notice Your Honour has directed our attention to the fact that the word Srebrenica erroneously appears in paragraph 68. It is not intended to include that in relation to Counts 4 and 5, deportation or inhumane acts and forcible transfer. We will attend to that in due course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I thank you for your clarification. Then I will put to the accused the counts of the indictment, then I would ask the accused to enter their pleas to each count I will put. Please confine your answer either guilty or not guilty to each count. If both of the accused could rise, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Count 1 of the amended indictment in relation to the added allegation in relation to Srebrenica alleges persecutions on political, racial, or religious grounds, a crime against humanity -- as a crime against humanity, which is punishable under Article 5(h) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Mr. Stanisic, how do you plead? THE ACCUSED STANISIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Simatovic, how do you plead? THE ACCUSED SIMATOVIC: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Count 2 alleges a murder as a crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 5(a) and 7(1) of the Statute. Mr. Stanisic, how do you plead? THE ACCUSED STANISIC: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Simatovic, how do you plead? THE ACCUSED SIMATOVIC: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Finally, Count 3, alleges a murder as a violation of the laws or customs of war, as recognised by Common Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions of 1949, punishable under Articles 3 and 7(1) of the Statute. Mr. Stanisic, how would you plea? THE ACCUSED STANISIC: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Simatovic, how do you plead? THE ACCUSED SIMATOVIC: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Please have a seat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'd like to note to the registrar that both accused have pled not guilty on all the new charges. That concludes our further appearance for today, but I wonder we can take this opportunity to use a part of Status Conference to discuss anything in relation to the case. The Chamber is currently seized of the motion challenging on the form of the indictment from the Defence and also this motion relating to the health of the accused. Is there -- the Chamber is considering this motion and will make its determination in due course. Apart from that, I wonder if there's anything for the parties to raise at this moment. Mr. Re?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There is just one small matter arising from the matter Your Honour mentioned of the challenge to the indictment or the amended indictment. Both accused have filed challenges. The challenge filed by the Defence for Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you speak up a bit or speak to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's these new microphones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Oh, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm just getting used to them. The Defence -- Defence counsel for both accused have filed separate challenges. Mr. Knoops for Mr. Stanisic has filed his publicly. Mr. Jovanovic has filed his confidentially. The Prosecution thinks that it might have been filed confidentially in error because there seems to be -- it's basically simply a legal challenge. Perhaps Mr. Jovanovic would be able to address Your Honour as to why there's any need for its confidentiality or whether it's been filed, as such, in error.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you for bringing that matter to my attention. Can I hear from Mr. Jovanovic on that issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. This morning I attempted to contact my learned friend to clarify this. In the preliminary Defence brief, the name of a witness is mentioned and part of a statement, which is confidential annex 5, and this was disclosed as part of the indictment. That is why --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters are finding it very hard to follow this. The sound is very poor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could I interrupt you, Mr. Jovanovic. Could you repeat the last part of your statement again, please. Could you start from "that is why."

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because in the preliminary objection in paragraph 16, the name of a witness is mentioned and part of that witness's statement. It was disclosed to the Defence as confidential annex B. This material is attached to the motion to amend the indictment, and it was disclosed to the Defence as part of annex B, which is confidential.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I take it, Mr. Jovanovic, from your statement that there would be no problem on your part to file a public version of your motion.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course, Your Honour. This morning I attempted to clarify this with Mr. Re. If the Prosecution does not object, the preliminary objection can be made public.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't see any reason why not, so could you do that as soon as practicable?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I will do this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Jovanovic. Mr. Re, can I hear about the status of disclosure in relation to these new charges?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The -- as far as I'm aware, all supporting material has been disclosed. Today, we have some further information from witness statements taken by the Belgrade -- the war crimes chamber of the Belgrade district court of witnesses to the incident relating to Srebrenica, the subject of the indictment we're disclosing to Mr. Jovanovic and Mr. Knoops. But that's the latest of it. It's up-to-date, as far as I know, as of today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Having heard that, is there anything to raise for the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. May I take this opportunity to address your Chamber also to be helpful to the Prosecution in relation to the motion on the fitness to stand trial. This afternoon, we have filed a reply to the Prosecution's response on the fitness of the accused to stand trial, and we noted that the Prosecution indicated in its response that the medical reports we refer to were not disclosed during the Status Conference of the 3rd of June, 2005. As we remember, we have filed these reports prior to the Status Conference as an addendum to the memorandum to prepare the Status Conference for Your Honour, but in addition to that these reports which were referred to in our initial motion were also attached as confidential annexes 1 and 2. So just to clarify that the motions we refer to as being submitted during or on behalf of the Status Conference of the 3rd of June last year were also appended as confidential annexes 1 and 2 to the current motion. I think this is further clarification, perhaps also for Your Honour, that these -- that these reports were also filed in support of the motion which lies now for Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you for the clarification, Mr. Knoops. So I take it there's no further issues to raise at this moment. Then the hearing is now adjourned.
